response_text: Pyridine-amide (N-(4-isopropoxyphenyl)isonicotinamide) lacks the classic strongly basic tertiary amine center typical of high-potency hERG blockers, as the pyridine nitrogen has a low pKa (~5.2) and remains largely unprotonated at physiological pH (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.48). However, the planar biaryl-like amide core and terminal hydrophobic isopropoxy group can still engage in hydrophobic and pi-stacking interactions with Tyr652 and Phe656 in the Kv11.1 inner cavity, resulting in weak-to-moderate micromolar inhibition (estimated IC50 ~18.5 uM, spanning the typical 10 uM binary classification threshold). In the Tox21 panel, metabolic O-dealkylation of the 4-isopropoxyanilide scaffold can generate p-aminophenol/quinone-imine intermediates that trigger the oxidative stress antioxidant response element (SR-ARE). Limitation: In silico QSAR models show higher uncertainty for neutral/weakly basic arylamides near the 10 uM cutoff. Recommendation: Conditional progression; confirm exact potency via GLP manual patch-clamp electrophysiology and evaluate reactive metabolite formation before Phase I.

Chlorobenzamide-morpholine (Moclobemide, ChEMBL:CHEMBL870) is a selective, reversible monoamine oxidase-A (MAO-A) inhibitor. Although it contains a 4-chlorophenyl ring linked to a basic morpholine ring, the morpholine nitrogen exhibits reduced basicity (pKa ~6.2) due to the inductive electron-withdrawing effect of the ring oxygen, and the molecule lacks the second distal hydrophobic aromatic group required for high-affinity multipoint binding inside the hERG inner cavity (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.22). Experimental patch-clamp and clinical studies confirm very weak hERG interaction with an IC50 > 50 uM (estimated ~85.0 uM; PMID:15974572), providing a wide safety margin at therapeutic free plasma concentrations, though QT prolongation has been noted in massive clinical overdose or comedication scenarios. Across the Tox21 high-throughput screening panel, moclobemide is inactive across nuclear receptor and stress response pathways. Limitation: Standard in vitro hERG assays do not capture pharmacodynamic drug-drug interactions. Recommendation: Proceed to clinical trials with standard ECG monitoring.

CF3-benzylpiperidine (4-[1-(4-trifluoromethylbenzyl)piperidin-4-yl]phenol) exemplifies the classic high-affinity hERG pharmacophore (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.94). It features a central protonatable tertiary piperidine amine (pKa ~9.2) flanked by a highly lipophilic para-trifluoromethylbenzyl group and a para-hydroxyphenyl ring at the optimal inter-aromatic distance to span the Kv11.1 inner pore. At physiological pH, the protonated piperidine forms strong cation-pi interactions with Tyr652, while the lipophilic CF3-phenyl moiety locks into hydrophobic pockets around Phe656, yielding sub-micromolar inhibition (estimated IC50 ~0.45 uM). In the Tox21 panel, its cationic amphiphilic structure causes mitochondrial membrane potential disruption (SR-MMP), while the 4-alkylphenol moiety mimics estradiol to activate Estrogen Receptor alpha pathways (NR-ER, NR-ER-LBD). Limitation: Predicted IC50 requires experimental patch-clamp verification and assessment of plasma protein binding. Recommendation: Do not proceed to clinical trials due to severe hERG cardiotoxicity risk and endocrine disruption liability.

Flavone-piperidine (7-(2-(piperidin-1-yl)ethoxy)-2-phenyl-4H-chromen-4-one) is a basic flavone derivative structurally analogous to flavoxate that strongly matches the canonical hERG blocker pharmacophore (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.89). The basic tertiary piperidine nitrogen (pKa ~9.5) connected via a flexible ethoxy linker to the rigid, planar 2-phenylchromen-4-one scaffold enables simultaneous cation-pi coordination with Tyr652 and deep pi-pi stacking of the flavone aromatic system with Phe656 in the hERG channel pore, resulting in potent inhibition (estimated IC50 ~1.2 uM). Within the Tox21 panel, the planar flavone core is a well-established ligand for the Aryl Hydrocarbon Receptor (NR-AhR) and exhibits weak phytoestrogen-like activity at the Estrogen Receptor (NR-ER), while the basic lipophilic amine drives mitochondrial membrane potential depolarization (SR-MMP). Limitation: Metabolic cleavage of the ethoxy linker in vivo could alter systemic exposure of the intact parent blocker. Recommendation: Do not proceed to clinical trials without scaffold redesign to attenuate hERG binding.

Aspirin (acetylsalicylic acid, ChEMBL:CHEMBL25) is a low-molecular-weight aromatic carboxylic acid (pKa ~3.5) that exists predominantly as a hydrophilic carboxylate anion at physiological pH 7.4 (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.01). The absence of a basic protonatable nitrogen and insufficient lipophilic bulk prevent entry into or stabilization within the hydrophobic inner cavity of the Kv11.1 channel, as electrostatic repulsion and desolvation penalties preclude interaction with Tyr652 and Phe656 (experimental IC50 > 100 uM, reported inactive at 100-1000 uM). In the Tox21 10K screening library, aspirin is completely inactive across nuclear receptor and cellular stress response assays up to 100 uM, acting selectively via cyclooxygenase (COX-1/COX-2) serine acetylation. Limitation: High-throughput in vitro screens do not capture gastrointestinal mucosal injury or platelet aggregation effects. Recommendation: Proceed; no hERG or Tox21 safety liabilities.

Caffeine (1,3,7-trimethylxanthine, ChEMBL:CHEMBL113) is a small, polar purine alkaloid lacking a protonatable basic amine at physiological pH (pKa < 1.0) and possessing low lipophilicity (LogP ~ -0.07) (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.02). Because it cannot form cation-pi interactions with Tyr652 or span the hydrophobic pockets around Phe656 in the Kv11.1 channel pore, it exhibits negligible hERG inhibition, requiring millimolar concentrations (IC50 > 1000 uM, ~3-5 mM; PMID:12142414) to affect cardiac potassium currents. In the Tox21 screening panel, caffeine is inactive across all nuclear receptor and stress response endpoints at standard screening concentrations (<= 100 uM). Limitation: Standard hERG and Tox21 panels do not reflect adenosine receptor antagonism or phosphodiesterase inhibition responsible for tachycardia at extreme doses. Recommendation: Proceed; completely clean hERG and Tox21 safety profile.

Ibuprofen (ChEMBL:CHEMBL521) is a propionic acid NSAID containing an acidic carboxylic group (pKa ~4.9) that is >99% ionized as a negatively charged anion at physiological pH 7.4 (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.02). Anionic compounds are electrostatically disfavored from entering the K+ conduction pathway and cannot engage in cation-pi interactions with Tyr652, nor does the single isobutylphenyl ring provide the multi-ring span needed to bridge Phe656 residues (IC50 > 100 uM; experimentally non-inhibitory in patch-clamp assays). Across the Tox21 high-throughput panel, ibuprofen shows no significant reproducible activation of nuclear receptors or stress pathways. Limitation: In vitro hERG and Tox21 assays do not model COX-mediated renal prostaglandin synthesis inhibition or long-term cardiovascular risk. Recommendation: Proceed; no cardiac ion channel or Tox21 liabilities.

Acetaminophen (paracetamol, ChEMBL:CHEMBL112) is a small, neutral p-aminophenol acetamide derivative (phenol pKa ~9.5, LogP ~0.46) completely devoid of a basic amine center or distal hydrophobic aromatic rings (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.02). Consequently, it cannot form cation-pi or extensive hydrophobic interactions within the hERG inner cavity and shows no hERG channel inhibition (IC50 > 100 uM, inactive > 300 uM). In the Tox21 panel, parent acetaminophen is largely quiescent because standard immortalized assay cell lines have low CYP2E1 metabolic capacity, though weak oxidative stress (SR-ARE) signaling can be observed at high micromolar concentrations due to trace formation of the electrophilic reactive metabolite NAPQI (N-acetyl-p-benzoquinone imine). Limitation: Standard Tox21 cell lines under-predict CYP-dependent hepatotoxicity at overdose levels. Recommendation: Proceed; safe regarding hERG and acceptable at therapeutic exposures.

Ethanol (ChEMBL:CHEMBL545) is a two-carbon aliphatic alcohol (MW 46.07 g/mol, LogP -0.31) lacking any aromatic rings, ionizable basic nitrogens, or steric bulk required to interact with the Kv11.1 channel pore residues Tyr652 and Phe656 (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.001). Patch-clamp electrophysiology demonstrates that ethanol only weakly modulates hERG currents at supraphysiological, intoxicant concentrations in the tens to hundreds of millimolar range (IC50 > 10,000 uM; PMID:16569708) via non-specific membrane fluidity perturbations. In the Tox21 screening panel (tested up to 100 uM), ethanol is completely inactive across all nuclear receptor and stress response assays. Limitation: Volatility and millimolar potency fall outside the dynamic range of micromolar high-throughput screens. Recommendation: Proceed; no micromolar hERG or Tox21 toxicity risk.

Metformin (1,1-dimethylbiguanide, ChEMBL:CHEMBL1431) is a strongly basic (pKa ~11.5), highly hydrophilic biguanide (LogP ~ -1.43) that exists as a hydrophilic cation at physiological pH (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.01). Despite carrying a positive charge, metformin completely lacks aromatic rings or hydrophobic moieties; the high thermodynamic desolvation penalty prevents it from shedding its hydration shell to enter the hydrophobic Kv11.1 inner cavity, and it cannot form pi-stacking interactions with Tyr652 or Phe656 (IC50 > 100 uM, inactive > 1000 uM). Across the Tox21 high-throughput screening panel, metformin is inactive across all 12 nuclear receptor and cellular stress pathway assays. Limitation: In vitro micromolar screens do not capture rare clinical lactic acidosis caused by millimolar hepatic mitochondrial Complex I inhibition in renal impairment. Recommendation: Proceed; devoid of hERG and Tox21 liabilities.

Ascorbic acid (Vitamin C, ChEMBL:CHEMBL196) is a highly water-soluble, polyhydroxylated gamma-lactone (LogP ~ -1.85) with an acidic enediol system (pKa1 ~4.17) that exists as the negatively charged ascorbate monoanion at physiological pH 7.4 (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.005). The combination of negative charge, dense hydrogen-bonding polarity, and total absence of basic nitrogens or aromatic rings precludes any binding to the hydrophobic pore residues (Tyr652, Phe656) of the hERG potassium channel (IC50 > 100 uM). In the Tox21 panel, ascorbic acid is an endogenous antioxidant and displays no adverse pathway activation across nuclear receptor or stress response assays. Limitation: High concentrations in cell media can occasionally cause assay-medium redox artifacts in vitro. Recommendation: Proceed; physiological nutrient with zero hERG or Tox21 safety concern.

Glucose (D-glucose, ChEMBL:CHEMBL1222250) is an endogenous hexose monosaccharide that is neutral, highly polar (LogP ~ -3.24), and heavily solvated in aqueous media (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.001). It possesses no protonatable amine groups and no aromatic or lipophilic structures capable of interacting with the Kv11.1 inner cavity residues Tyr652 and Phe656, resulting in complete inactivity at the hERG channel (IC50 > 1000 uM; standard bath solutions routinely contain 5-10 mM glucose without inhibiting hERG currents). Similarly, glucose is completely inactive across all Tox21 nuclear receptor and stress response assays. Limitation: None relevant to direct chemical toxicity at physiological concentrations. Recommendation: Proceed; completely safe endogenous carbohydrate.

Penicillin G (benzylpenicillin, ChEMBL:CHEMBL29) is a beta-lactam antibiotic containing a polar bicyclic penam core and a carboxylic acid group (pKa ~2.7) that is fully ionized as a carboxylate anion at physiological pH 7.4 (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.02). Although it contains a single benzyl side chain, the net negative charge and absence of a basic amine prevent electrostatic attraction or cation-pi binding in the Kv11.1 inner pore, yielding no significant hERG inhibition (IC50 > 100 uM, experimentally inactive > 300 uM). In the Tox21 panel, Penicillin G specifically targets bacterial peptidoglycan transpeptidases and is inactive across all mammalian nuclear receptor and stress response pathways. Limitation: In vitro Tox21 and hERG assays do not predict IgE-mediated hypersensitivity or anaphylactic reactions in sensitized patients. Recommendation: Proceed; clean cardiac and cellular toxicity profile.

Gallic acid (3,4,5-trihydroxybenzoic acid, ChEMBL:CHEMBL288114) is a small, polar phenolic acid (pKa ~4.4, LogP ~0.70) that exists as a carboxylate anion at physiological pH and lacks any basic nitrogen center or extended hydrophobic scaffold (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.01). Consequently, it cannot access or bind the hydrophobic Phe656/Tyr652 binding pocket of the hERG channel (IC50 > 100 uM). In the Tox21 panel, however, the pyrogallol (1,2,3-trihydroxybenzene) moiety readily undergoes auto-oxidation and redox cycling in aerobic cell culture media to generate semiquinone radicals, ortho-quinones, and hydrogen peroxide, which activate the Nrf2 antioxidant response element (SR-ARE) and DNA damage/p53 stress pathways (SR-p53) at micromolar concentrations. Limitation: In vitro catechol/pyrogallol auto-oxidation in cell culture media often exaggerates stress pathway activation compared to in vivo systemic conditions where rapid glucuronidation/sulfation occurs. Recommendation: Proceed; devoid of hERG risk, with in vitro Tox21 stress flags attributable to known polyphenol redox cycling.

Ferulic acid (4-hydroxy-3-methoxycinnamic acid, ChEMBL:CHEMBL32749) is a dietary hydroxycinnamic acid containing an ionizable carboxylic acid group (pKa ~4.58) and a single guaiacol-like aromatic ring without any basic amine moiety (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.02). Being negatively charged at physiological pH 7.4 and lacking a protonatable nitrogen or a second distal hydrophobic ring, ferulic acid does not inhibit the hERG channel (IC50 > 100 uM). In the Tox21 panel, its conjugated alpha,beta-unsaturated carboxylic acid and para-hydroxy-meta-methoxyphenyl system can act as a weak Michael acceptor/redox modulator that mildly induces Nrf2-mediated antioxidant response signaling (SR-ARE) at high concentrations, without cytotoxicity or nuclear receptor disruption. Limitation: High phase II metabolic clearance in vivo limits systemic free parent drug levels. Recommendation: Proceed; safe non-blocker with benign dietary phytochemical profile.

Succinic acid (butanedioic acid, ChEMBL:CHEMBL576) is a small endogenous four-carbon dicarboxylic acid (pKa1 ~4.2, pKa2 ~5.6, LogP ~ -0.59) that exists as the doubly negatively charged succinate dianion at physiological pH 7.4 and serves as a central intermediate in the mitochondrial tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle (predicted hERG blocking probability: 0.001). Devoid of aromatic rings, lipophilic bulk, or positively charged nitrogens, succinate is strongly repelled from the K+ channel pore and exhibits zero hERG liability (IC50 > 1000 uM). In the Tox21 screening panel, succinic acid is completely inactive across all nuclear receptor and stress response assays. Limitation: None; commonly used as a pharmaceutically acceptable salt counterion (succinate salts). Recommendation: Proceed; completely safe endogenous metabolite.
